guidance.heading: Installation: do’s and don’ts
guidance.text: Eight points from the catalogue. In the drawings, red marks the mistake and blue marks the right way.

items.title: Do not twist the hose
items.text: Pressure applied to a twisted hose can result in hose failure or loosening of connections.

items.title: Allow slack for length change
items.text: When a hose is installed straight, leave enough slack to provide for the length changes that occur when pressure is applied.

items.title: Keep bend radii as large as possible
items.text: To avoid hose collapse and flow restriction, refer to the hose specification tables for minimum bend radii.

items.title: Use proper angle adaptors
items.text: Angle adaptors avoid a sharp twist or bend in the hose.

items.title: Allow adequate hose length
items.text: Enough length distributes movement on flexing applications and avoids abrasion.

items.title: Use elbows and adaptors to relieve strain
items.text: They give neater installations that are more accessible for inspection and maintenance.

items.title: Bend in the plane of the motion
items.text: Prevent twisting and distortion by bending the hose in the same plane as the motion of the part it connects to.

items.title: Avoid rubbing and abrasion
items.text: Route hose away from moving parts. Clamps of the correct size can support long runs; a loose clamp lets the hose move inside it and causes abrasion.
